correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the full positive SIRS system, f(I)>=f(0)>0, strict log drift threshold, and covariance PSD hypotheses. Total N has uniformly bounded second moment since quadratic variation density <=QN^2 and Q<2mu, yielding boundary/martingale strong laws. The balance equations bound average susceptible population by Lambda/mu and force exponential I extinction. Positive recovered variation of constants and the same-noise linear susceptible X yield exponentially decaying R and S-X; local Lipschitz f^{-1} makes the nonlinear incidence error time-integrable. Affine X has ergodic mean m, moment q and X_t/sqrt(t)->0 in probability. Integration of dX gives an exact log I martingale decomposition with bracket slope v_rho. The continuous martingale CLT and strong law prove both limits; correlation minimization is an exact completed-square identity. Edge cases a=0 or b=0 and rho=±1 are included, not critical lambda=0 or Q>=2mu. Direct independent symbolic rationals rechecked the moments and variance floor; no simulation is offered as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The stochastic epidemic source provides an extinction upper exponent and sensitivity about a positive endemic equilibrium; these do not imply an exact time-asymptotic log-extinction CLT. The result published on the same source about a nondegenerate boundary susceptible law identifies X’s inverse-gamma stationary behavior but not the infection fluctuation variance/correlation floor. Related SIRS and stochastic epidemic fluctuation papers address varying population, many-particle limits or extinction times. The exact claimed process-level limit remained uncovered in inspected statements; unpublished or unindexed stochastic boundary CLTs remain a genuine risk.
residual_risks: Older unindexed diffusion CLTs near extinction might contain an equivalent fixed-noise logarithmic limit.
Huang et al. claim disease-free susceptible point convergence under positive multiplicative noise, known to be false; current proof instead couples to a fluctuating boundary diffusion.
Martingale and pathwise moment arguments were mathematically reconstructed, not independently formalized.

value.rationale: The strict extinction criterion predicts sign, not the distribution of long-time log-infection uncertainty. A closed variance with a sharp attainable correlation floor distinguishes first-order threshold robustness from second-order extinction risk and gives a motivated stochastic-epidemic asymptotic rather than a normalization check.
